section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the statistical analysis procedures: IBM SPSS v.22 was used for descriptive and Pearson correlation analyses and AMOS v.22 for path analysis. Path analyses (Maximum Likelihood) tested whether social safeness predicts disordered eating via self-reassurance and body appreciation while controlling for BMI, with model fit indices (χ2/df, CFI, TLI, RMSEA) and bootstrap (5000 samples, 95% CI) used to evaluate effects and significance.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'The Software IBM SPSS (v.22: SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL) was used to perform descriptive and correlational analyses, and path analysis was conducted using the software AMOS (Analysis of Momentary Structure, v.22; SPSS Inc., Chicago IL). ... Finally, path analyses were conducted to test whether the association between social safeness (exogenous variable) and disordered eating attitudes and behaviours ... would be mediated by self-reassurance and body appreciation (endogenous mediator variables) while controlling for BMI.'
